name: Cursor
product: AI-native code editor combining code generation, repository context, agentic tool use and model routing.
targetCustomer: Individual software developers and enterprise engineering organizations
buyer: Developer, CTO or VP Engineering
latestRound: Series D, Nov 2025 ($2.3B); pending SpaceX acquisition announced Jun 2026
traction: Cursor reported more than $1B in annualized revenue and millions of developers in Nov 2025; SpaceX announced a pending $60B acquisition in Jun 2026.
notes: Pending acquisition materially changes its value as a standalone comparable. Funding is a rounded sum of announced rounds; revenue and usage are company-reported.

name: Cognition
product: Devin autonomous software-engineering agent and Windsurf agentic IDE for completing multi-step coding tasks.
targetCustomer: Software teams and large enterprises
buyer: CTO, CIO or VP Engineering
traction: Cognition reported a $492M revenue run rate in May 2026 and more than 10x enterprise-usage growth since the start of 2026.
notes: Funding total comes from a secondary aggregate; revenue and usage are self-reported. Windsurf integration expands distribution but adds integration risk and exposure to frontier-model economics.

name: Replit
product: Browser-based agentic platform that turns natural-language specifications into running, tested and deployed applications.
targetCustomer: Non-technical builders, developers and enterprise teams
buyer: Individual builder, business-unit leader, CIO or CTO
traction: Replit reported adoption at 85% of the Fortune 500 in Mar 2026; in Sep 2025 it reported $150M annualized revenue, 40M users and 500,000 professional users.
notes: Cumulative funding is estimated by adding the $400M 2026 round to PitchBook's roughly $478M post-2025 estimate. The integrated build-run-deploy wedge is strong; reliability, unit economics and billing predictability remain material risks.

name: Poolside
product: Enterprise software-engineering agents backed by code-specialized models and deployable in customer-controlled environments.
targetCustomer: Large and regulated enterprise engineering organizations
buyer: CIO, CTO or VP Engineering
traction: Poolside launched an enterprise platform in May 2026 with VPC, on-premise and air-gapped deployment; current revenue and customer-count metrics were not publicly disclosed.
notes: Deep model-plus-runtime stack is technically differentiated, but commercial traction is not quantified and frontier-model training makes the thesis highly capital-intensive.

name: Magic
product: Research-led company building ultra-long-context code models intended to act as autonomous software-engineering coworkers.
targetCustomer: Software developers and enterprise engineering teams
buyer: CTO or VP Engineering
traction: Magic announced work toward 100M-token context windows and a large Google Cloud training system in 2024; no current revenue, broad product availability or customer metric was found.
notes: Substantial research capital does not yet establish product-market fit. Differentiation is vulnerable if long context and coding capability commoditize before a product and distribution wedge emerge.

name: Augment Code
product: Enterprise coding assistant and agent with a context engine designed for large, multi-repository codebases.
targetCustomer: Professional developers in medium and large engineering organizations
buyer: CTO, VP Engineering or developer-productivity leader
traction: Augment publicly launched its context-engine-driven coding product in 2024; no recent revenue or independently verified adoption metric was found.
notes: Enterprise codebase context is a credible wedge, but repository retrieval and model routing are rapidly commoditizing. Current commercial scale remains unknown.

name: Factory
product: Droids and Missions coordinate coding agents across planning, implementation, review, testing and maintenance workflows.
targetCustomer: Enterprise software-engineering organizations
buyer: CTO, CIO or VP Engineering
traction: Factory reported hundreds of thousands of daily developers and six consecutive months of more than 2x month-over-month revenue growth in Apr 2026.
notes: Model-agnostic workflow integration is a useful enterprise position; adoption and growth claims are company-reported, and differentiation against IDE agents is still falsifiable through retention and task-completion data.

name: Qodo
hq: New York, USA / Tel Aviv, Israel
subsector: AI code review and software quality
product: Multi-agent code-review, test-generation and quality platform focused on verifying code throughout the development lifecycle.
targetCustomer: Software developers and enterprise engineering teams
buyer: VP Engineering, application-security leader or developer-productivity leader
traction: Qodo reported 1M IDE installs and 20,000 pull requests reviewed per day at the end of 2024; current paid usage was not disclosed.
notes: Code integrity is a sharper wedge than generic completion, but coding vendors can bundle review and tests. The critical moat test is whether proprietary review feedback improves measurable defect escape rates.

name: LangChain
product: Open-source LangChain and LangGraph frameworks plus LangSmith for tracing, evaluation, deployment and management of agents.
targetCustomer: AI application developers and enterprise AI platform teams
buyer: Developer, Head of AI or AI-platform leader
traction: LangChain named Replit, Clay, Harvey, Rippling, Cloudflare, Workday and Cisco as customers in Oct 2025.
notes: Open-source reach is the principal distribution moat; durable monetization depends on LangSmith becoming a system of record rather than a replaceable framework layer. Funding total is the sum of publicly reported seed, Series A and Series B rounds.

name: LlamaIndex
subsector: Enterprise knowledge agents and document processing
product: Open-source agent framework and commercial platform for extracting, indexing and acting on enterprise documents and knowledge.
targetCustomer: AI developers and enterprise data or automation teams
buyer: Head of AI, data-platform leader or CTO
fundingDisplay: $27.5M disclosed before later undisclosed strategic investments
traction: LlamaIndex's company profile reports more than 25M monthly SDK downloads and use at Fortune 50 companies; methodology and paid conversion are not disclosed.
notes: Strong open-source distribution and document specialization are credible wedges, but the RAG and orchestration stack is crowded and composable. Funding excludes undisclosed strategic investments.

name: Browserbase
subsector: Managed browser runtime for AI agents
product: Managed Chromium infrastructure with sessions, identities, proxies, observability and agent APIs for reliable web automation.
targetCustomer: Developers and companies building browser-using agents
buyer: Developer, Head of AI or engineering-platform leader
traction: Browserbase's company profile reports more than 35M browser sessions per month and 300,000 Hyperagent sessions since Apr 2026.
notes: Purpose-built browser infrastructure can compound operational know-how, but browser vendors, hyperscalers and anti-bot controls constrain defensibility and create policy risk. Usage is company-reported.

name: E2B
product: Open-source, isolated microVM sandboxes that let AI agents execute code and operate computers with API-level lifecycle controls.
targetCustomer: Developers and enterprises building code-generating or computer-using agents
buyer: Developer, Head of AI or platform-engineering leader
traction: E2B reported that 88% of the Fortune 100 had signed up and that hundreds of millions of sandboxes had been created by Jul 2025; signup is not equivalent to paid deployment.
notes: Execution isolation is a hard requirement for agents and a strong infrastructure wedge. Cloud commoditization, security liability and hyperscaler competition are the main risks.

sources.label: Series A, cumulative funding and usage

name: Composio
product: Integration platform providing authenticated tools, action schemas, routing and reusable skills for AI agents.
targetCustomer: Developers and AI-native product teams building tool-using agents
buyer: Developer, Head of AI or engineering-platform leader
traction: Composio's company profile claims its integrations power more than 1M AI-native teams; no methodology, revenue or paid-customer count was disclosed.
notes: Connector depth and accumulated tool-use feedback could compound, but integrations are labor-intensive and replicable. Authentication makes security and supply-chain trust existential product requirements.

name: Pydantic
product: Pydantic AI framework and Logfire platform for typed agent development, tracing, evaluation and model-gateway operations.
targetCustomer: Python developers and enterprise AI engineering teams
buyer: Developer, Head of AI or platform-engineering leader
traction: At company formation, Pydantic reported roughly 40M monthly package downloads; that open-source distribution is the main commercial wedge for Logfire and Pydantic AI.
notes: A ubiquitous Python validation library creates exceptional developer distribution, but paid conversion and differentiation in crowded observability and agent-framework markets remain unproven.

name: Arize AI
product: Enterprise observability and evaluation platform for machine-learning, LLM and agent systems, paired with the open-source Phoenix project.
targetCustomer: ML engineers, AI engineers and enterprise AI platform teams
buyer: Head of AI, ML-platform leader or Chief Data Officer
traction: Arize reported more than 2M monthly Phoenix downloads when announcing its Series C in Feb 2025.
notes: Phoenix creates an open-source distribution wedge and cross-model telemetry can become a system of record. The category is crowded and cloud or APM incumbents can bundle adjacent capabilities.

name: Braintrust
product: Evaluation, tracing, datasets, scorers and production-feedback platform for teams shipping LLM and agent applications.
targetCustomer: AI engineers and product teams operating production AI applications
buyer: Head of AI, engineering leader or product leader
traction: Braintrust names Notion, Replit, Cloudflare, Ramp and Dropbox among customers in its Feb 2026 Series B announcement.
notes: Eval-first workflows and production feedback can create sticky datasets, but observability is crowded and automated evaluator reliability remains a technical ceiling.

sources.label: Series A and prior cumulative funding

name: Galileo
product: Evaluation, observability and guardrail platform for testing and monitoring generative-AI and agent applications.
targetCustomer: Enterprise AI teams deploying generative-AI applications
buyer: Head of AI, Chief Data Officer or ML-platform leader
latestRound: Acquired by Cisco, completed May 2026; last funding Series B, Oct 2024 ($45M)
traction: Galileo reported 834% ARR growth in 2024, six Fortune 50 customers and 400% growth in new customers before its acquisition by Cisco.
notes: Cisco completed the acquisition in May 2026, so Galileo is no longer an independent startup target. The exit validates observability demand, while reported operating metrics remain vendor-provided.

sources.label: Series B, cumulative funding and metrics
Cisco acquisition announcement and completion update

name: Patronus AI
subsector: Agent evaluation, red teaming and simulation
product: Platform for evaluating, red-teaming and training agents with automated evaluators and digital-world simulations.
targetCustomer: Frontier AI labs and enterprises deploying high-stakes agents
buyer: Head of AI, AI safety leader or ML-platform leader
traction: Patronus reported 15x revenue growth over the prior year when announcing its Jun 2026 Series B; absolute revenue was not disclosed.
notes: Digital-world simulations could turn eval data into training infrastructure, but this expands scope and capital needs. Revenue growth is self-reported without an absolute base.

sources.label: Series B, cumulative funding and metrics

name: Giskard
product: Open-source and enterprise platform for automated red teaming, evaluation and security testing of LLM and agent systems.
targetCustomer: European enterprises and regulated organizations deploying LLM applications
buyer: CISO, Head of AI, model-risk leader or Chief Data Officer
traction: Giskard names AXA, BNP Paribas and Michelin as customers and reports research collaboration and benchmarking work with Google DeepMind.
notes: Relevant French control point with an EU regulatory wedge, but capitalization and global distribution trail larger competitors. Public descriptions mix equity funding, grants and support, so no USD total is asserted.

name: Lakera
subsector: Runtime security and red teaming for generative AI
product: Lakera Guard detects prompt injection, data leakage and unsafe model interactions at runtime, complemented by red-team data from Gandalf.
targetCustomer: Enterprises deploying generative-AI applications and agents
buyer: CISO, Head of AI or application-security leader
latestRound: Acquired by Check Point, completed Oct 2025; last funding Series A, Jul 2024 ($20M)
traction: Check Point acquired Lakera in 2025 to add AI-native security to its platform; Lakera is therefore no longer an independent company.
notes: Gandalf supplies valuable adversarial interaction data and security research credibility, but benchmark and latency claims are vendor-reported. Acquisition removes it from the standalone startup set while validating the category.
